walkthroughs.body_html:
Geographic Perspectives: Global Change (Population Distribution, Global Climate, Global Resource Consumption) — a core area of Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Geographic Perspectives: Global Change (Population Distribution, Global Climate, Global Resource Consumption) brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Geographic Perspectives: Global Change (Population Distribution, Global Climate, Global Resource Consumption).

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: A megacity is an urban area with more than how many people?
options: 10 million
1 million
5 million
100 million

mcqs.q: Which factor best explains low population density in the Sahara?
options: A hot arid climate limits water supply and farming
It is too mountainous for any settlement
Governments ban people from living there
It lies outside any country's territory

mcqs.q: Climate change vulnerability depends on exposure, sensitivity and what else?
options: Adaptive capacity
Latitude only
Population size only
Wind direction
The interdependence of water, food and energy resources
A global trade agreement
A type of hydroelectric dam
A United Nations headquarters building

mcqs.q: Is the world's population spread fairly evenly across the land?
options: No - distribution is highly uneven: huge concentrations occur in South and East Asia and in coastal lowlands, while deserts, high mountains and polar areas are sparsely populated.
Ecological footprint measures the size of a person's shoes.
Most of the world's people live in the polar regions.
People are spread roughly evenly, so a country's population just reflects its size.

mcqs.q: Do the countries that emit the most greenhouse gases suffer the most from climate change?
options: Whoever causes the most emissions automatically experiences the worst impacts.
Climate change only affects countries on the Equator.
Not necessarily - many low-income countries emit little but are highly vulnerable because of exposure and low adaptive capacity, while high emitters often have more resources to adapt.
Most of the world's people live in the polar regions.

mcqs.q: Does ecological overshoot mean Earth's resources are already used up?
options: Ecological footprint measures the size of a person's shoes.
Climate change only affects countries on the Equator.
No - it means humanity's annual demand exceeds the planet's annual biocapacity, so we are drawing down natural capital, which is unsustainable over time.
Overshoot means resources are completely exhausted right now.
